response.rationale: R3 integrates antipsychotic exposure, fever, rigidity, tachycardia, and elevated CPK/liver enzymes, matching NMS as a drug-induced emergency. R2 captures only catatonic motor signs, which are correlated restatements also present in NMS and therefore less discriminative. R1 rests solely on the splenial MRI lesion but is disconfirmed by the explicit absence of hyponatremia or metabolic derangement and by the reversible nature of the lesion.

rejected.why: Osmotic demyelination is not supported because the vignette states no hyponatremia and no metabolic disorder; the single splenial finding with complete resolution is outweighed by the fever, rigidity, tachycardia, and CPK elevation characteristic of the champion.
